title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 21-23): M is a poset of 'multiplicités' (model strata, multi-strata). L is an ambient set of 'points'. Each X in M has a subset L_X = {x in L : x << X}, and X -> L_X is increasing. Condition 3 on p.21 introduced the 'open stratum' L°_X = L_X minus the union of the L_{X'} over X' < X, and required it to be non-empty. A 'figure' F ⊂ M is a family of mutually compatible multiplicities, roughly a complex built from models; one sets L_F = union of the L_X for X in F.

On this page:
(1) Completion of the argument begun on p.21. Take x in L_X. Since M_{≤X} is finite (well-founded), there is an X_i ≤ X that is minimal among the Y ≤ X with x in L_Y. Then x lies in L°_{X_i}, so L_X is the union of the L°_{X_i} for X_i ≤ X. More precisely, x is in L°_{X_i} exactly when X_i is minimal among the Y ≤ X with x in L_Y.
(2) Desideratum. The minimal element should be unique, i.e. a least element. Equivalently, distinct X_i, X_j ≤ X have disjoint open strata, so that L_X is the DISJOINT union of its open strata. More generally, for a figure F, L_F should be the disjoint union of the L°_X for X in F. Equivalently, every x in L_F has a smallest X in F with x in L_X.
(3) Condition 4. If X ≠ Y are compatible (contained in a common figure), then L°_X ∩ L°_Y = ∅. Restated: if x is in L_X ∩ L_Y, then x already lies in L_{X'} for some X' < X and in L_{Y'} for some Y' < Y.
(4) Margin: for compatible X, Y this is equivalent to L_X ∩ L_Y = union of the L_Z over Z ≤ X, Z ≤ Y. This is exactly the 'intersection is a union of common faces' axiom for fans and polyhedral or regular cell complexes.
(5) A struck-out converse question: if all open strata of elements below X and Y are pairwise disjoint, are X and Y compatible?

Purpose: axiomatizing the combinatorial skeleton of tame/stratified 'analysis situs'. The figure's support is partitioned into open strata indexed by the face poset. The next page draws the consequences: the scholie with injectivity of X -> L_X and the equivalence X ≤ Y iff L_X ⊂ L_Y iff L°_X ∩ L_Y ≠ ∅.
errors: The existence of a minimal X_i uses finiteness or well-foundedness of M_{≤X}; this is assumed, as indicated by the parenthetical remark.

The margin equivalence holds when the intersection formula is required for all pairs within the figure. This includes pairs of faces, which inherit compatibility. The equivalence is then correct: one direction by uniqueness of the open stratum containing x, the other because Z ≤ X, Y with Z = X would force X < Y, contradicting x in L°_Y.
The struck-out final question is left unanswered.

ideas.what: Open strata L°_X = L_X minus the union of the L_{X'} over X' < X, with L_X the union of the open strata of its faces
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified set; relative interiors of faces in a cell or polyhedral complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Whitney/Thom stratifications; regular CW complexes; face posets)
ideas.where_published: spirit of Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures); not in this axiomatic form

ideas.what: Condition: compatible distinct multi-strata have disjoint open strata, equivalently L_X ∩ L_Y is the union of the L_Z over common faces Z
ideas.modern_name: fan / polyhedral complex intersection axiom; strata partition
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in toric geometry (Demazure, Kempf-Knudsen-Mumford-Saint-Donat) and PL topology

ideas.what: Characterization: x lies in L°_X iff X is minimal among the faces whose L contains x; uniqueness of the minimal element gives disjointness
ideas.modern_name: carrier / support face of a point
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (carrier of a point in a simplicial complex)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorial axiomatics: partition of a support into open strata indexed by a face poset, plus the fan-type intersection axiom. It is a natural step in Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology draft but contains nothing absent from standard theory.
transcription_corrections: 'Conj 4' is probably 'Cond 4' (condition), continuing 'Cond 3' of p.21; the next page's 'Cor 3, Cor 4' likely also means 'Cond 3, Cond 4'.
'(ici comme dans un convexe[?] du X fini)' is uncertain; the sense is 'as in the finite case', i.e. M_{≤X} finite so minimal elements exist.
'parmi ces transversaux[?]' is likely 'parmi ces X_i' / 'parmi les Y tels que...'.
